meta.title: FEAT-006 · Sign in with an email code
meta.subtitle: Design solution from technical-design.md: request a 6-digit code by email, then sign in with it. Pick a flow to follow one UC-029 path; click any arrow for its data contract.
meta.description: The visitor enters an email on SCR-STF-021. Identity refuses a second request for the same address within 60 seconds (429 with Retry-After), otherwise ends every open challenge of the address, stores a new challenge with only the hash of a fresh code and, when an account exists, queues SignInCodeRequested so Notification emails the code. An unknown address gets the same 201 and a real challenge, but no email. On SCR-STF-022 the visitor types the code: an ended or expired challenge is refused, a locked account is refused without comparing the code, a wrong code counts on the challenge (ended at the fifth) and on the account lockout in one save, and a correct code ends the challenge, verifies an unverified email, clears the lockout and signs the user into hs.idp (amr=otp) exactly like a password sign-in. All of it sits behind the gateway's existing 10-per-minute-per-IP auth limiter.
overview: POST /v1/users/sign-in/code-challenges, POST /v1/users/sign-in/code, event SignInCodeRequested/v1, Retry-After on ApiException
new table sign_in_code_challenges (xmin, partial unique open index); audit method code

nodes.label: Browser
nodes.desc: The visitor. After a code sign-in holds hs.idp with pwd_at (when the account has a password), auth_time and amr=otp; then the BFF cookie after the authorize round trip.

nodes.label: Storefront SPA
nodes.desc: SCR-STF-012: "Sign in with an email code" link keeping returnUrl. SCR-STF-021 /signin/code: email, 429 countdown from Retry-After. SCR-STF-022 /signin/code/enter: six digit boxes with paste, resend countdown, wrong / expired / ended / locked states; challenge kept in sessionStorage (never the code). Serves the seller centre too, through the hosted /signin.

nodes.label: Gateway + BFF
nodes.desc: Route users (/v1/users/{**rest}) with policy auth: one 10-per-minute window per client IP shared by all /v1/users* calls (FEAT-005). Over it: 429 common.rate_limited with Retry-After. Relays /connect/authorize and runs the BFF callback after the code sign-in.

nodes.label: Identity
nodes.desc: Domain: SignInCodeChallenge, SignInCodePolicy (6 digits, 5 min, 60 s, 5 wrong). Application: RequestSignInCodeHandler, SignInWithCodeHandler (one save per attempt, bounded retry), LockoutRecorder.Stage*. Infrastructure: SignInCodeGenerator (CSPRNG, SHA-256 salted with the id, FixedTimeEquals), SignInChallengeSweeper (1 day). Api: two endpoints under /v1/users/sign-in/.

nodes.label: identitydb
nodes.desc: New sign_in_code_challenges: id, email_hash, user_id (null for an unknown address), code_hash, failed_count 0..5, created_at, expires_at, ended_at, end_reason (used / superseded / attempts), xmin; unique open challenge per email_hash. audit_entries.method gains code. No plain email, no code.

nodes.label: Service Bus
nodes.desc: Outbox relay, at least once. Carries SignInCodeRequested/v1 only for addresses that have an account.

nodes.label: Notification
nodes.desc: Validates SignInCodeRequested (pydantic, extra=forbid), upserts the contact, writes one email_records row and renders sign_in_code.{vi,en} with the code and "valid for 5 minutes". The body is never stored or logged.

nodes.label: Email provider
nodes.desc: SMTP. Delivers the code email to the visitor's inbox.

data.p: Email on SCR-STF-021; six digits on SCR-STF-022
data.s: The code lives only in the input; never stored by the SPA

data.p: POST /v1/users/sign-in/code-challenges {email} · POST /v1/users/sign-in/code {challengeId, code, returnUrl} · then GET /connect/authorize… and the BFF callback
data.s: Responses: 201 {challengeId, expiresAt, resendAvailableAt}; 200 {redirectUrl} + hs.idp; 400; 401 sign_in_code_invalid / sign_in_code_expired / sign_in_challenge_ended; 423 account_locked; 429 sign_in_code_too_soon or rate_limited + Retry-After
data.w: Over 10/min per IP: rejected here, Identity not called

data.p: The same requests; hs.idp passes through
Newest challenge for email_hash (60 s rule); end open challenges (superseded); insert challenge with code_hash; outbox SignInCodeRequested when an account exists
data.s: Only hashes stored; open-index conflict → 429 too soon, Retry-After 60
data.w: Unknown address: same rows, no outbox row

data.p: Challenge by id and lockout row; wrong: failed_count+1 on both (challenge ends at 5); correct: end challenge (used), verify email, delete lockout; audit row method code
data.f: EF Core · one SaveChanges per attempt
data.s: xmin conflicts on challenge or lockout → reload and reapply (bounded); constant-time compare

data.p: SignInCodeRequested/v1 {userId, email, displayName, language, code, expiresAt}
data.s: Carries the code (R-6, as VerificationEmailRequested); never logged; 5-minute lifetime

all.title: FEAT-006 design solution
all.intro: Request a code, sign in with it, and the exception paths: too soon or resend, wrong or expired code, locked account, unknown address.

steps.t: Enter email on SCR-STF-021; POST /v1/users/sign-in/code-challenges through the per-IP limiter.
Issue: earlier open challenges end (superseded); a new challenge stores only SHA-256(id ‖ code); 201 {challengeId, expiresAt, resendAvailableAt}.
Email with the code arrives; SCR-STF-022 shows the entry and the resend countdown.
Type or paste the code; POST /v1/users/sign-in/code {challengeId, code, returnUrl}.
Correct: in one save the challenge ends used, an unverified email is verified, the lockout row is deleted, sign_in_succeeded (method code) is written.
200 {redirectUrl} with hs.idp (pwd_at when there is a password, amr=otp); the browser goes through /connect/authorize and the BFF callback back to where it came from.
Within 60 s of the last request for the address: 429 identity.sign_in_code_too_soon with Retry-After; nothing written. Also for unknown addresses.
After 60 s: a new code; the previous challenge is ended and its code stops working.
Wrong code: +1 on the challenge and on the account lockout in one save; 401 identity.sign_in_code_invalid.
Fifth wrong code: the challenge ends (attempts); 401 identity.sign_in_challenge_ended, request a new code.
Expired: 401 identity.sign_in_code_expired, not counted. The bodies never reveal whether the email exists.
Locked (by passwords and codes together): 423 identity.account_locked without comparing the code; audit sign_in_failed. Password and Google sign-in are offered.
Same 201 and a real challenge with a code that is never sent; no outbox row, no email.
Any code gets the same 401 answers as for a real account, ending at the fifth.

notes.t: A real challenge for every address
notes.b: Unknown addresses get a stored, expiring, countable challenge with an unsent code, so every response is identical by construction.
Covered by the existing auth route and limiter; submit answers like signIn. The challenge id stays out of URLs.

notes.t: Email only as a hash, purged after a day
notes.b: The 60 s rule needs per-address memory even for unknown addresses; NFR-LEG-001 keeps the clear address out. HMAC rejected for one-day rows.

notes.t: Locked accounts still get a code
notes.b: Refusing the request would make it a lock oracle (FR-AUTH-029); the submit is refused (FR-AUTH-035).

notes.t: Challenge and lockout in one save
notes.b: LockoutRecorder gains staging methods so a wrong code counts on both, also under parallel submits.
With the outbox (ADR-0002) Identity cannot know at request time; the code page always offers resend and password/Google. UC-029 2b rewording proposed.
Lifetime, five tries, lockout and the IP limit guard the code; argon2 would add latency without changing that.
FEAT-004's exact pwd_at rule would reject the cookie otherwise; set-password re-auth still means Google.
Lockout, audit, limiter and Retry-After exist only on feat/005-account-hardening. Merge first.
Add "sign-in code challenge" to Identity in §5.2 and SignInCodeRequested to §5.4 events (software-architecture).
